title: Randomized noise contraction
statement: For every real $q>1$, there is a real number $c$ with $0<c\le1$, and with $c=2/5$ whenever $q=4$ or $q=4/3$, such that for every $n$, every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, and every real-valued function $f$ on its outcome space, the $q$-moment norm of the randomization of the product noise operator with parameter $c$ applied to $f$ is at most the product $q$-moment norm of $f$: $\|R(T_cf)\|_q\le\|f\|_{q,P}$.
hypotheses_covered: If q = 4 or q = 4/3, then c = 2/5
P is a product of n finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
f is a real-valued function on the product outcome space
replaced: For every $q>1$ there exists $0<c\le1$, with $c=2/5$ if $q\in\{4,4/3\}$, such that for every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and every real $f$ on its outcome space, $(\mathbb E_{x\sim P}\mathbb E_r|R_r(T_cf)(x)|^q)^{1/q}\le\|f\|_{q,P}$, where $r$ is uniform on the Boolean cube. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$ for $r\in\{0,1\}^n$; $R_rh=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\chi_S(r)h_S$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
